title: Dynamic operator ensemble kernel selector for mixed-length workloads
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Goal: build an online+offline autotuner that picks the best kernel implementation (attention + operator kernels) per request class using architecture and sequence-length fingerprints. The selector should minimize tail latency violations under latency SLOs while keeping cost within configured budgets. It must consider prefill vs decode trade-offs and be safe for production rollouts (canary, quick rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Selector integrates with runtime scheduling and returns a kernel candidate for each incoming inference request within 200 microseconds of decision time
End-to-end median and p95 latency improvements for heterogeneous seq-len workloads compared to current baseline: >=6% median, >=10% p95 on mixed production traces
No increase in inference error modes (OOMs, retries) in canary cluster compared to baseline
Automated warm-start from offline microbenchmark DB and ongoing online microprobes enabled
Can roll out via existing runtime rollout APIs with canary and auto-fallback policies
design_decisions: Two-tier approach: offline fingerprint catalogue + lightweight online probe/estimator. Offline DB provides warm-start and priors; online probes refine performance model under real contention and input distributions.
Use a hybrid cost model combining token/sec throughput, per-token compute cost estimate, and a latency tail penalty term. The cost model weights are configurable per-customer SLO tier.
Sequence-length bucketing: inputs are mapped to coarse buckets (e.g., 0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) to reduce state explosion while preserving relevant behavior for kernel choice.

Attention kernel selection: prefer FlashAttention variants for >128 seq with supported GPU arch; use blockwise/custom kernels for small seq lengths on lower occupancy to save memory and reduce latency.

Prefill vs decode: make distinct policies — prefill can benefit from larger batch kernels, decode favors low-latency kernels and KV cache-friendly implementations. Policy composes based on request phase.
Exploration strategy: epsilon-decay bandit with safety constraints (limit exploration to <=5% of traffic per model/route), plus scheduled microprobe bursts during low-traffic periods.
Fallback policy: if runtime detects repeated errors or latency regressions from selected kernel, immediately switch to pre-configured stable kernel and emit alert with diagnostics.
Decision latency target: selection logic must add <0.2ms overhead in fast path; heavy model fitting runs are done asynchronously.
Telemetry: surface per-kernel request counts, median/p95 latency, GPU occupancy, and estimated cost delta in Console dashboards and per-route traces.
Security: no customer data is sent to external services; fingerprints are derived from sequence length, model id, and architecture only.
technical_notes: Offline microbenchmark DB schema: (model_id, arch_fingerprint, kernel_id, seq_bucket, batch_size) -> perf metrics (tokens/sec, median_ms, p95_ms, mem_peak_mb)
Warm-start pipeline: nightly microbench runs across representative models and archs; results ingested into DB and exposed via local replicated cache on each runtime node.

Online probe design: lightweight prefill microprobe piggybacks on first unit requests for new model/version; uses synthetic small-budgetbursts (<=10 requests) to evaluate candidate kernels under live contention.
Cost model formula (simplified): score = latency_penalty * p95_ms + alpha * (1 / tokens_per_second) + beta * mem_peak_mb; alpha/beta/latency_penalty are tunable by tier.
Integration points: selector API hooks into request admission pipeline right after model/version lookup and before batching. Exposes recommended kernel and optional suggested batch size.
Data retention: microprobe traces retained for 30 days for model-specific calibration; aggregated per-arch stats retained for 180 days.
Canary workflow: tag 2% of traffic for candidate kernel routing; monitor latency and error rates for 24h with automated rollback if p95 increases >10% or error rate > 0.2%.
Test harness: use production trace replay (sanitized) in staging to validate selector behaviors across seq-len mixes.
Dependencies: requires latest kernel registry (kernels-service v1.9+) and runtime-telemetry v3.1 to annotate per-request kernel choice metrics.

Open question: how granular should arch_fingerprint be? (CUDA compute capability vs device model vs driver/kernel version). Current plan: start with compute capability + memory size bucket, iterate if needed.

risks: Exploration causing regressions: even limited randomized probing can affect tail latency if probes land on hot nodes. Mitigation: limit probe rate, prefer underloaded nodes, and run probes with lower priority.
DB staleness: offline microbenchmarks may not reflect runtime contention or newer driver/kernel patches. Mitigation: replicate nightly probes and prioritize recent online telemetry.
Complexity increase: more decision logic in fast path risks adding jitter. Mitigation: keep selection deterministic for common buckets and perform heavy model updates off-path.
Memory/regression risks from some kernel variants (OOMs) under high batch sizes. Mitigation: reject candidates that exceed a conservative mem_peak threshold in DB for a given arch.
Observability gaps: if per-request kernel tags are missing, debugging regressions is harder. Mitigation: require telemetry annotation in PR before rollout.
